Cyber Attack Disrupts Jordan’s Industrial Intermediate Prod Firms, Operations Halted at Multiple Sites

Amman – A coordinated cyber attack targeting the Industrial Intermediate Prod sector in Jordan has led to sweeping operational disruptions across several major firms, with production lines halted and workers idled at key facilities. The incident, which began in the early hours of Wednesday, has been described by company representatives and industry bodies as one of the most significant cyber threats to hit the sector in recent years.

According to sources within the Jordan Intermediate Manufacturers Association, at least eight firms have been affected so far, including Al-Majd Intermediates and Petra Processed Inputs, among others. The attack, believed to be ransomware deployed through compromised IT systems, forced plant managers to execute emergency shutdown procedures at multiple sites in Amman, Zarqa, and Irbid.

“Initial indications suggest that the attackers gained access to central control systems, encrypting critical production data and demanding payment for its release,” said Khaled Abu Nawas, spokesperson for the association. “Our immediate priority has been ensuring the safety of our workers and the integrity of our facilities.”

Production workers arriving for early shifts found access denied at several sites, with security and IT personnel turning away staff as a precaution. “We received instructions not to clock in until further notice,” said a machine operator at a plant in the King Abdullah II Industrial Estate, who asked not to be named. “Everyone is worried about the impact on our wages and whether the systems will be restored soon.”

Industry analysts estimate that daily output losses across the affected firms could exceed JOD 2 million if the disruption continues through the end of the week. “The Industrial Intermediate Prod sector is a backbone of Jordan’s manufacturing supply chain, and any prolonged halt is likely to have a significant effect on its own operations,” said Lina Al-Sabah, an industrial economist in Amman.

As of Thursday afternoon, IT teams at the impacted companies are working with cyber security consultants to restore system access and assess the extent of the breach. Union representatives have called for transparent communication with workers regarding timelines for resuming operations and measures to protect employee income during the ongoing disruption.
